pageTitle: Klacks for large businesses | No license per head
metaDescription: Klacks for businesses with over 250 employees: no license per employee, no user fees, no subscription. Roles, group visibility, LDAP/OIDC, payroll export.
hero.title: No license per head. No license fees under the AGPL.
hero.subtitle: No license per employee, no user fees, no subscription — with 2,000 people the maths works out differently than with 20.
costs.title: What costs money — and what does not
costs.none.title: Not applicable with Klacks
costs.paid.title: Costs on your side
costs.paid.items.0: Server or hosting — in-house or with a provider of your choice
costs.paid.items.1: Operation and maintenance by your IT team or a service provider
costs.paid.items.2: The AI model: external providers bill by usage, a model you run yourself needs suitable hardware
costs.paid.items.3: The rollout: taking over data, setting up rules, training schedulers
costs.note: We deliberately do not name a saving in percent: what you save depends on what you pay per head today.
features.title: What large businesses need — and what Klacks can do today
features.roles.title: Roles and rights
features.roles.text: Administration with all rights, supervisor without deleting and settings. Schedulers without a further role may read, record assignments, absences and notes, and use Klacksy.
features.visibility.title: Visibility by group
features.visibility.text: You define per user who sees which groups. Schedulers then only see the employees of their groups; the administration sees everything. Employees without a group remain visible to everyone.
features.identity.title: Sign-in through your directory
features.identity.text: Sign-in via LDAP or Active Directory as well as via OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0. You take over employees by synchronising with LDAP or Active Directory, which you trigger in the settings.
features.payroll.title: Payroll export
features.payroll.text: At period closing, Klacks creates the payroll export as a file — among others for DATEV and Abacus, as well as CSV or Excel.
features.import.title: Import from Excel or CSV
features.import.text: You import employees from an Excel or CSV file; a preview shows what is missing before anything is saved.
features.audit.title: Traceability
features.audit.text: Every record stores who created it, last changed it or deleted it, and when. Period closings, reopenings with a stated reason and daily approvals are kept in a separate log.
features.approval.title: Approval levels
features.approval.text: Assignments can be confirmed, approved and closed; each level locks editing.
features.updates.title: Signed, automatic updates
features.updates.text: The installation package comes with an update service that applies signed new versions of server and interface together.
features.scale.title: Tested with a large dataset
features.scale.text: Klacks was developed and tested with a dataset of 5,000 employees.
agents.title: Your AI agents work directly with Klacks
agents.text: Klacks comes with its own MCP server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard through which AI agents work with software. Any agent that supports MCP — such as Claude, Cursor or your own agents — can use it to work directly with Klacks: with the tools Klacksy uses as well, and only with the rights of the connected user.
agents.steps.0.title: Create an access token
agents.steps.0.text: An administrator creates a personal access token in Klacks under Settings › System (with the “Expert mode” switch turned on), in the “Personal Access Tokens” section. Agents that support OAuth 2.1 sign in with a Klacks account instead.
agents.steps.1.title: Enter the MCP server in the agent
agents.steps.1.text: Your IT team makes your installation's MCP server reachable at https://<your-domain>/mcp. You enter this address and the token in your agent as an MCP server.
agents.steps.2.title: Work with the user's rights
agents.steps.2.text: The agent sees and changes only what the user who owns the token may — and never more than a supervisor, even if the token belongs to an administrator.
agents.items.0: Sign-in by login token, personal access token or OAuth 2.1.
agents.items.1: Operating steps in the interface and sensitive functions, such as creating access tokens, are locked through the interface.
agents.items.2: The interface also provides the Klacks documentation and ready-made workflows to the agent.
requirements.title: What you should know
requirements.items.0: Klacks is not a cloud solution: you handle hosting and operation yourself, or a service provider of your choice does.
requirements.items.1: We recommend a Linux server with Docker Engine. Docker Desktop (Windows, Mac) requires a paid license for companies with 250 or more employees or 10 million USD or more in annual revenue.
requirements.items.2: The installation package requires at least 8 GB of memory and 4 CPU cores.
requirements.items.3: One installation represents one company with one company time zone. You model locations and departments through groups.
klacksy.title: Klacksy does not replace schedulers — Klacksy takes over the clicking
klacksy.text: Forming groups, setting up scenarios, recording entries: by sentence, with a preview and only after your yes. The rule-based planning engine calculates the plan. It takes the stored rules into account – rest times, qualifications, hour limits – and shows violations before anything takes effect. What only planners know – who can be reached at night, who cannot be asked for a shift right now – is not in the system. That is why you decide.
klacksy.modelText: Klacks provides Klacksy with its capabilities. You decide which AI model sits behind it: from a provider of your choice or on your own server. Klacks helps you find a suitable model: a built-in test shows whether it works for Klacksy.
cta.title: Check it with your IT team
cta.text: The source code is public, the Playground is open: your IT team can check Klacks before we talk to each other.
